column3: NASB renders “the other” as “his neighbor.”
NASB follows the critical text (“Or”); “unworthy of the smallest cases” is rendered “not competent to constitute the smallest law courts.”
NASB renders “Surely not ever” as “How much more.”
NASB takes the verse as a question (“do you appoint them as judges”); it can also be read as a command, and the meaning is uncertain.
NASB follows the critical text; “For shame to you” is rendered “to your shame,” and “his brother” is “his brethren.”
NASB renders the verse as a question.
NASB follows the critical text without “in”; “suffer wrong” is rendered “be wronged.”
NASB follows the critical text; “brothers” is rendered “brethren.”
NASB renders “the sexually immoral” as “fornicators.”
NASB follows the critical text.
NASB follows the critical text without “our” and with “Christ”; “by the Spirit” is rendered “in the Spirit.”
NASB renders “do profit” as “are profitable.”
NASB renders “belly” as “stomach,” “destroy” as “do away with,” and “sexual immorality” as “immorality.”
NASB adds “not only … but also.”
NASB renders “a prostitute” as “a harlot” and “having taken” as “take away.”
NASB renders “prostitute” as “harlot,” adds “with her,” and renders “it says” as “He says”; the quotation is in capitals.
NASB adds “with Him.”
NASB adds “other” and renders “sexual immorality” as “immorality” and “the one sinning sexually” as “the immoral man.”
Close to the Greek.
NASB follows the critical text without the Textus Receptus words “and in your spirit, which are God's.” A full-width colon appears in the NASB text.
